statements.text: Earlier this year, NIST released the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework, RMF, a voluntary framework to guide organizations and incorporating trustworthiness into the design, development, and deployment of AI systems. [...] How will NIST ensure these efforts to advance trustworthy AI are deployed into real-world use by stakeholders?
statements.context: House committee hearing on the NIST FY 2024 budget proposal, where a member questions the agency on AI framework deployment.

statements.text: I've seen instances where overregulation hinders our ability to compete globally, thereby forcing growth overseas or allowing others to step in and lead. [...] So, Dr. Murdick, how do we make sure that we do not overregulate, but rather innovate through the facilitation of bottom-up, consensus-based standards rather than top-down regulations?
statements.context: Rep. Brian Babin questions a witness at a House hearing on AI and national interest.

statements.text: The American research enterprise currently operates in a transparent and open manner with basic research being published without restrictions. [...] How can we maintain a balance between ensuring the openness of basic AI research, while also mitigating potential threats to national security that might arise from sharing such information?
statements.context: Congressional hearing titled 'Artificial Intelligence: Advancing Innovation Towards the National Interest,' where Rep. Babin questions expert witnesses.

statements.text: AI has the potential to bolster our defenses for critical infrastructure like the Port of Houston, but it can also be an asset for nefarious actors as well. [...] develop and promote AI policies that will safeguard our critical infrastructure, including major ports like the Port of Houston?
statements.context: House Science, Space, and Technology Committee hearing on AI risk management, featuring testimony from NIST and other witnesses.

statements.text: by many metrics, China has caught up and in many cases surpassed the United States in research and commercial capabilities. Chinese universities are publishing many more research papers than U.S. institutions. [...] How concerned are you with the pace of AI progress in China?
statements.context: House hearing on AI risk management where Rep. Babin questions a panel of witnesses about China's AI progress.

statements.text: I think that this is a cutting-edge development that if we fail to take the lead—or keep our lead, I should say, I think we are in the lead right now—but we have adversaries that are absolutely intent on replacing and supplanting us as the No. 1 power, and AI is going to be huge.
statements.context: House committee budget hearing for the 119th Congress.

statements.text: And what has Jacksonville's experience with AI been in your transit system, and how would you recommend other agencies adopt it to make their systems safer and more efficient?
statements.context: House committee hearing on US transit policy where a lawmaker questions a municipal transit official about AI adoption and data-security practices.

statements.text: We have put together some very robust cybersecurity programs and testing, in terms of testing those systems for penetration and things of that nature.
statements.context: House hearing on America's transit policies and programs, featuring a Member questioning a Jacksonville transit official about AI and data security.

statements.text: And, then, to maintain a competitive advantage over our bad actors, like the Chinese Communist Party, President Trump has emphasized the need to build, baby, build across the U.S. economy and our critical infrastructure. And from your perspective, Director Kratsios, what elements of the AI Action Plan most effectively strengthen the U.S. economy and position the United States as the global leader in AI?
statements.context: Hearing on the U.S. AI Action Plan before a congressional committee.

statements.text: Congress must ensure that America leads in AI. And doing so will bolster our economic competitiveness, protect our national security, and promote our values of liberties and freedom.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Chairman Babin at a House Science, Space, and Technology Committee hearing on the Trump Administration's AI Action Plan.

statements.text: the time to use artificial intelligence in business is now, and we must do everything we can to support small business efforts to harness the power of this technology.
statements.context: Floor remarks in the U.S. House urging passage of the Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act (H.R. 3679).

statements.text: This legislation directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology, or NIST, to develop and share practical resources to help small businesses better understand and adopt artificial intelligence technologies.
statements.context: Floor statement in the House of Representatives in support of H.R. 3679, the Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act.

statements.text: Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the bill (H.R. 3679) to require the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop resources for small businesses in utilizing artificial intelligence, and for other purposes, as amended.
statements.context: Floor consideration in the House of Representatives of H.R. 3679, the Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act, under suspension of the rules.

statements.text: Permitting delays for power generation and transmission, environmental review bottlenecks, and regulatory uncertainty slow the construction and expansion of critical infrastructure.
statements.context: Opening statement at a House Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee hearing on federal permitting challenges for data center infrastructure.

statements.text: Madam Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the bill (H.R. 3029) to amend the Research and Development, Competition, and Innovation Act to support nucleic acid screening, and for other purposes, as amended.
statements.context: Floor debate in the House of Representatives on suspending the rules to pass H.R. 3029, the Nucleic Acid Standards for Biosecurity Act.

statements.text: Executive Order 14409 hardens our systems against AI-enabled cyberattacks by partnering with American industry rather than regulating it into the ground.
statements.context: Opening statement by Chairman Brian Babin at a House Science Committee hearing on FY2027 research and technology priorities, featuring testimony from OSTP Director Kratsios.
